_doc: Source of truth for the /start/ four-corner diagnostic. Three radio questions (leak, stage, paperwork) route a visitor to one of seven named journeys, each surfacing 3-5 library articles + 1-2 tools + 1-2 sheets + 3-5 glossary terms (the four corners of a complete read-watch-do-define kit). The /start/ page reads this file at build time; the result HTML is rendered client-side from the journeys object after the visitor submits the form. A miss (no tuple matches) falls back to the fallback block. EN/ES parity is handled at render time: journey titles + headlines + the question/option strings translate via parallel files; the library/tool/sheet/glossary slugs themselves are shared (EN ↔ ES is resolved through data/i18n-slug-map.json). When you edit this file: (1) every slug referenced must exist on disk under library/, tools/, sheets/, or glossary/; (2) the verification block in the integration agent's runbook will fail CI if any slug is broken; (3) bump _lastReviewed and note the change in the canon doc (docs/start-here-canon.md §3).

questions.help: The thing keeping you up. Pick the closest one.

options.head: Margin / cash flow
options.dek: Sales are fine but the bank account isn't.

options.head: Online discovery
options.dek: Google, Maps, and mobile aren't doing their job.

options.head: Kitchen / menu
options.dek: Plate cost, recipe drift, the menu itself.

options.head: I don't know yet
options.dek: Give me one composite read and a starting point.

questions.legend: 2. Where is the restaurant right now?
questions.help: Pick the closest. There's no wrong answer.

options.head: Building from scratch
options.dek: No site yet, or the one we have needs tearing down.

options.head: Open and running
options.dek: Doors are open. Operations are real. Something's drifting.

options.head: Rebuilding or scaling
options.dek: Open, but the back office or the digital surface needs an overhaul.

questions.legend: 3. What records do you have on hand?
questions.help: P&L, recipes, invoices. Honest answer only — this picks whether the right next step is a calculator or a sheet.

options.head: I can pull last month's numbers
options.dek: Sales, food cost, labor — within a few points.

options.head: Some of it, not all
options.dek: Recipes exist for the top sellers; the P&L is rough.

margin-with-numbers.title: Margin's bleeding, and you have the numbers.
margin-with-numbers.dek: The calculators can fire. Run the prime-cost band first, then the menu math, then the channel math.
margin-with-numbers.headline: Read these in order. The prime-cost band tells you whether the leak is food, labor, or both.

margin-no-numbers.title: Margin's bleeding, but the records aren't there yet.
margin-no-numbers.dek: The calculators can't fire until the paperwork does. Two sheets first, then the math.
margin-no-numbers.headline: Fill the sheets for two weeks first. The calculators are useless without the inputs.

covers-thin.title: Covers are thin. The room isn't full.
covers-thin.dek: Covers leak from three places: the menu doesn't convert, the site doesn't rank, or the door isn't findable. Test in that order.
covers-thin.headline: Start at the storefront score. The weakest layer is where the covers go.

discovery-dark.title: Discovery is dark. Google isn't pulling its weight.
discovery-dark.dek: Local SEO is sequenced: Google Business Profile first (it dominates local intent), then mobile + speed, then titles + schema.
discovery-dark.headline: Open the GBP grader first. The Map Pack is where most of the covers come from.

kitchen-menu.title: You suspect the menu, not the marketing.
kitchen-menu.dek: Kitchen-side fixes pay back in margin and brand. Plate-cost first, then how it photographs, then how it reads.
kitchen-menu.headline: Cost the plate first. Every menu decision under it is a guess otherwise.

building-from-scratch.title: Just opened, or building from scratch.
building-from-scratch.dek: No site, or the one you have needs tearing down. Read the structural posts first; the calculators come after the foundations.
building-from-scratch.headline: Read the structural posts first. The platform call and the brand system carry every page after.

unsure-composite.title: Not sure yet. Give me one read.
unsure-composite.dek: One composite check, one score, one starting point. The audit infers what it can; you pick the next room from there.
unsure-composite.headline: Run the storefront score first. Read the score, then come back and pick the right journey.

fallback._doc: Returned when the answer tuple matches no journey. The five most universally useful items across the library — the structural starting set for any independent restaurant operator.
fallback.title: Start with the foundations.
fallback.dek: These four corners cover the structural ground for any independent restaurant — the site, the listing, the menu, the math.
fallback.headline: Read these in order. The four corners are the same regardless of which leak shows up first.
